Bridge.co redesign · phase 2 · chosen direction

The reference style, applied to two homepages

Distilled from the approved exploration: letterspaced BRIDGE wordmark, serif display type, deep navy with dusk photography, caps microtype, deal callouts, and a navy stat band. Below is the style reference extracted from those comps, then full-scroll builds of the two selected heroes: Candidate A replicates variant 1 (The Funded Object) and Candidate B replicates variant 4 (Two Doors). Everything below the hero is byte-for-byte identical between them, built from one shared file, so the hero is the only variable in the comparison.

Photography is real and embedded in the page (openly licensed Unsplash shots, graded navy to match the reference). Treat them as high-fidelity placeholders: final art should be licensed or shot for Bridge. Deal figures and stats are carried over from the reference and should be verified before launch.

Style reference · extracted from the approved comps

One system, six rules

Serif speaks, sans organizes, navy holds the room, amber is only ever light in a photograph, numbers are the loudest thing on the page, and everything else stays quiet.

Photography direction

Hotel at dusk
Construction in progress
Product on the shelf
  • Dusk and golden hour, graded toward navy. Warm light is earned by the photograph, never by the UI.
  • Work in progress over finished glamour. Cranes, PIPs, pallets, people in their place of work. No stock cliches.

Voice

  • Lead with a financed object, not a promise. A real amount, a real asset, Bridge’s role stated plainly.
  • Short declaratives. "Built for what’s next." "Financed." Nothing needs a second clause.
  • Caps microtype carries the facts. Role, status, category. If it’s data, it’s small, spaced and uppercase.
  • The numbers do the persuading. $2.5B+, 1,000+ transactions, 24 days, 96% repeat. Adjectives stay home.
Candidate A · replicated from variant 1

The funded object

One brand, one hero, and a real deal doing the talking. The $75M construction loan carries the promise; the two businesses are routed one scroll down.

Reading the comparison

Same system, different first move

Everything from the stat band down is identical on purpose, generated from a single shared file, so the decision is purely about the hero: A leads with one brand and one proof deal, then routes at "Two kinds of builders"; B routes instantly and proves inside each door. If traffic splits evenly between the two audiences, B converts the sure-footed visitor faster; A builds the single Bridge brand harder and handles the undecided visitor better.

To productionize: swap placeholder scenes for licensed photography per the art direction notes, confirm the display serif license, and verify every figure with capital markets before launch.
